title: Observation of gravity-like signatures in holographic codes on a quantum computer
authors: Debopriyo Biswas, Gong Cheng, Krishnanand Karthikeyan, Diana Muñoz-Valencia, Vincent P. Su, Hrant Gharibyan, Daiwei Zhu, Grant Salton, Evgeny Epifanovsky, Martin Roetteler, Christopher Monroe, John Preskill, Norbert M. Linke, ChunJun Cao, Crystal Noel
abstract: The unification of quantum mechanics and general relativity remains one of the major open problems of theoretical physics. The Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence provides a valuable theoretical framework for this effort via a holographic duality between a theory of quantum gravity in asymptotically AdS spacetime and a conformal quantum field theory on the lower-dimensional boundary. Here, we implement a toy model of this duality called the HaPPY code, a quantum error-correcting code in the form of a tensor network with hyperbolic entanglement patterns, on a trapped-ion quantum computer. We present the first experimental confirmation of the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena formula in this model - a key test of the holographic correspondence. We then enrich it with non-stabilizerness, or magic, and observe entropic precursors expected of emergent gravity. Finally, we present and measure a code construction whose entropic behavior is reminiscent of a highly quantum wormhole. Our experiments illustrate how quantum computers can serve as testbeds for modeling the emergence of spacetime.
summary: The research uses trapped-ion quantum computers to experimentally model the AdS/CFT correspondence via holographic error-correcting codes. By measuring entanglement entropy, they first verified a key formula relating entanglement to area (FLM) and then showed that introducing non-stabilizer resources generates state-dependent signatures predicted by theories of emergent gravity. This work establishes quantum computation as a novel platform for testing fundamental physics conjectures.
main_problem: The central problem is unifying quantum mechanics and general relativity by investigating whether spacetime geometry emerges from fundamental quantum entanglement degrees of freedom.
main_result: The authors experimentally confirmed the Faulkner-Lewkowycz-Maldacena formula using a holographic code model, and further demonstrated that introducing non-stabilizer resources leads to state-dependent entropy signatures analogous to gravitational backreaction.
method: They implemented toy models of AdS/CFT duality (holographic codes) on a trapped-ion quantum computer, measuring entanglement entropies to calculate 'proto-area entropy' ($	ext{SPA}$).
model_or_system: The system uses the HaPPY code, a tensor network realizing a quantum error-correcting code, implemented on a trapped-ion platform. The model is extended by injecting non-stabilizer resources ('magic') to simulate gravitational backreaction effects.
key_observables: Proto-area entropy ($	ext{SPA}$), boundary entanglement entropy ($S_A$), recovered bulk entropy ($S_a$), and the dependence of $	ext{SPA}$ on bulk entanglement ($	heta$).
important_parameters: The entangling angle ($	heta$) controlling bulk entanglement, and the magic parameter ($M$) quantifying non-stabilizerness.
main_assumptions: The observed effects are interpreted as modeling emergent spacetime geometry, but the authors caution that this is a toy model and not a literal probe of semi-classical gravity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the HaPPY code structure, compare measured $	ext{SPA}$ vs. theory predictions for FLM testing, and show how increasing bulk entanglement ($	heta$) causes $	ext{SPA}$ to change when magic resources are added.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the experimental realization of the holographic duality test (FLM formula). It then enriches the model with non-stabilizerness ('magic') to observe state-dependent signatures, culminating in analogies involving wormhole geometries and two-sided entanglement structures.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum computation hardware (trapped ions) with fundamental physics problems (quantum gravity), providing an experimental testbed for concepts like holographic duality and emergent spacetime geometry that are highly relevant to AMO physicists studying complex many-body dynamics.

In the wormhole analogy (top right), boundary-anchored geodesics, shown in blue, pass through the neck connecting the two sides. (Bottom) increasing the inter-code entanglement decreases the effective wormhole length, thereby shortening this candidate geodesic and reducing the geometric contribution to the entropy in sufficiently short wormholes in holography. Red curves denote the boundary subregions.
